what_worked: Consistent visual template with readable typography and clear slide hierarchy.
fix_next: This is a generic AI thought-leadership pitch, not a data-story presentation—use the assigned dataset and show actual analysis.
verdict: No dataset analysis whatsoever; this is a consulting pitch deck, not a data story.
factual_error_detail: No claims from the assigned dataset are made, so no dataset-specific errors to count, but the entire deck fails to engage the assignment.

evidence.insight: Zero slides reference the 1,000-row dataset. No original analysis, no findings, no metrics derived from data. Every claim is generic industry commentary (e.g., '$15.7 trillion PwC projection,' '60% of knowledge worker time').
evidence.narrative: The deck follows a coherent consulting-pitch arc (problem → opportunity → roadmap) but this narrative has nothing to do with a data-story assignment. No thesis grounded in data. Slides 5 and 10 repeat the same 'lead or follow' rhetorical question.
evidence.framing: No audience, question, or context tied to the assigned dataset. No mention of the dataset's scope (1,000 companies, 30-day revenue, payment providers, categories). A cold reader would not know this was a data-analysis assignment.
evidence.accuracy: Cannot be assessed against the dataset because no dataset claims are made. External claims (PwC $15.7T, ChatGPT 100M users in 2 months) are plausible but unverifiable here and irrelevant to the assignment.
